authority: #K2-450 sec.2.4 (adopted means). READ-ONLY: reading the consumer corrected my own R1414 hand-off. Zero exam runs.

what_the_consumer_actually_does.code: if net in _CH: _c = _CH[net]; for _w in (0, ...): mr.WALL_RECT = (_c[0]-_w, _c[1]-_w, _c[2]+_w, _c[3]+_w); sol, why = orig(...)
what_the_consumer_actually_does.meaning: the channel is applied as the solve DOMAIN (a single WALL_RECT) for that net - it is NOT a per-point check.

correction_to_R1414: R1414 said the consumer edit is 'treat _CH[net] as a list; a point in corridor k may only use slot k'. That was too optimistic: there is no per-point check to amend - the solve domain is ONE rect, so 'one net = one rect' is baked into the SOLVER's domain interface.

therefore_per_corridor_requires_one_of.detail: make the maze's domain model accept a list of rects (or a polygon) so a net's domain can be the union of its corridor slots; the maze's inside-test must consult all rects.
keep the single-rect interface and invoke the solve once per (net, corridor) with that corridor's slot as WALL_RECT, stitching the pieces; the chain issues N extra calls.

recommendation: option (ii) is the smaller change to the frozen maze internals: it reuses the existing single-rect domain verbatim and only changes the CALLER's loop (the chain), at the price of more solve calls. Option (i) touches the maze's core inside-test.
status: the allocator half is complete and green (R1406/R1408/R1410/R1412); the maze-side half needs one of the two options above, which is a design decision plus a bounded implementation.
